newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Product Swaps - Gas oil down on supply worries.
newsitem.headline: Asia Product Swaps - Gas oil down on supply worries.

text.p: Singapore gas oil swaps were down at midday on Friday due to fears of a prompt physical overhang amid weaker overnight crude, traders said.
"Gas oil is under some pressure because the endusers are not buying and stocks in Singapore and around the region are high," one trader said.

Traders said while the steep contango is making it worthwhile for oil companies to keep gas oil and jet fuel in storage, they are also being forced to sell part of the oil at discounts to spot quotes to make room for new production.
The gas oil market is steady in the absence of fresh indicators in a fairly quiet trade.
September was last quoted 10 cents lower from Thursday at $23.20/$23.30 per barrel with one lot traded at $23.25, brokers said.
October was also quoted 10 cents lower, leaving the September/October spread unchanged at minus 60 cents. October traded this morning at $23.95, they said.
Traders said concerns of an oversupply were raised again due to the re-emergence of five sellers on the spot market on Thursday.
Physical cargoes for early September were offered down to a low of $22.60 or at 30 cents below Singapore spot quotes with no buyers coming out against it.
Naphtha also fell despite the crude hike as concerns over the high stocks led to a sell-off. September was last quoted at $21.25/$21.45 per barrel, down from Thursday's $21.40/$21.60, brokers said.
But fuel oil baulked the downward trend and put on between 25 and 50 cents on expectations of physical support and a prompt tightness.
September fuel oil swaps were last quoted at $104.75/$105.50 per tonne, up from Thursday's $104.50/$105.00, brokers said.
